title: Hidden-target navigation — find the beacon by local sight
description: A meadow crossed by a stone wall. Somewhere in it stands a beacon, out of sight from where you start. You see only what is near you.
goal: Find the beacon and stand on its cell. You are not told where it is: it appears in your view as an item of type 'beacon' once it is within sight. A stone wall may lie in the way.
notes: Design (not shown to agents as a map): Single agent. A beacon (a ground item) stands somewhere in a 24x24 meadow; it is out of sight at the start, and a stone wall lies between. Nothing in the prompt or goal says where the beacon is: it appears in the agent's view only once within the view radius. Success = standing on the beacon's cell. Built for the Yeoul/LxM connectome comparison (hub-ops 149/093): an agent that sees only locally, with the same observation and actions for a rule baseline, a connectome controller and an LLM.
Target and start are 14 cells apart in x; the beacon is beyond the default view radius (5) at start.
The wall at x=11, y=2..14 forces a detour (the rim y<2 and the meadow y>14 are open).
Seeded variants (start, target, walls) come from lxm/envs/blockworld_env.py: layout_for_seed(); this file is seed=None.
Movement is on z=1; trees (wood at z=1) in the SW corner are obstacles too; north/south move along y (rules.md).
